"PROJECT ETERIA

COMPLETE 3D FANTASY MMORPG – GAME DEVELOPMENT BLUEPRINT

Create an ambitious, immersive, 3D fantasy MMORPG called PROJECT ETERIA.

The game takes inspiration from the freedom, exploration, hidden content and progression systems of Shangri-La Frontier and Satisfy (Overgeared), but must have its own original universe, characters, creatures, locations, mechanics and lore.

IMPORTANT:
This must be designed as an actual playable video game, not a concept, static environment, visual presentation or interactive mockup.

Prioritize functional gameplay systems over descriptions of features that do not actually work.

==================================================

1. CORE GAME PHILOSOPHY
   ==================================================

Create a persistent fantasy world where players can develop completely different identities.

There must be no mandatory gameplay path.

Players should be able to become:

- Warriors.
- Mages.
- Assassins.
- Archers.
- Summoners.
- Beast tamers.
- Merchants.
- Blacksmiths.
- Alchemists.
- Explorers.
- Adventurers.
- Guild leaders.
- Territory rulers.

Combat must not be the only meaningful activity.

Every profession must have its own progression, rewards and opportunities.

The world must not revolve around a single protagonist.

==================================================
2. OPEN WORLD

Create a gigantic fantasy continent called ETERIA.

The world should contain:

- Large medieval kingdoms.
- Independent cities.
- Small villages.
- Ancient forests.
- Snow-covered mountains.
- Deserts.
- Swamps.
- Underground civilizations.
- Oceans and islands.
- Abandoned castles.
- Ancient temples.
- Hidden dungeons.
- Dangerous unexplored territories.

Each region must have its own ecosystem, inhabitants, resources, monsters and environmental identity.

Implement:

- Day and night cycles.
- Dynamic weather.
- Different environmental conditions.
- Wildlife.
- Enemy territories.
- Discoverable locations.
- Hidden treasures.
- Environmental storytelling.

Exploration should reward curiosity.

Do not fill the world with repetitive generic activities.

==================================================
3. CHARACTER CREATION

Create a detailed character creation system.

Allow players to customize:

- Appearance.
- Hair.
- Face.
- Body proportions.
- Starting equipment.
- Name.

Character appearance must be independent of combat specialization.

Players must be able to change equipment visually without necessarily changing their character identity.

==================================================
4. CLASS AND SKILL SYSTEM

One of the most important systems in ETERIA.

Do not force players to select a permanent class at the beginning.

Instead, allow their actions and achievements to influence their development.

Examples:

A player who frequently fights with swords may unlock advanced sword techniques.

A player who studies magic may develop magical specialization.

A player who spends time crafting may discover unique crafting professions.

A player who explores dangerous territories may unlock exploration-related titles and abilities.

Create:

- Basic skills.
- Advanced skills.
- Unique skills.
- Hidden skills.
- Legendary skills.
- Secret classes.
- Evolutionary class paths.

Some classes must require rare and difficult conditions.

Examples of original secret classes:

- Abyssal Knight.
- Dragon Sovereign.
- Void Architect.
- Phantom Monarch.
- Eternal Spellblade.
- Beast King.

These classes must be discovered through gameplay, not simply selected from a menu.

==================================================
5. COMBAT SYSTEM

Implement a real-time action combat system.

Combat must include:

- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Combos.
- Dodging.
- Blocking.
- Parrying.
- Special abilities.
- Weapon-specific attacks.
- Skill cooldowns.
- Mana consumption.
- Enemy attack patterns.

Different weapons must create genuinely different fighting styles.

Weapons:

- Swords.
- Greatswords.
- Daggers.
- Spears.
- Axes.
- Bows.
- Staves.
- Dual weapons.
- Shields.

Combat must reward timing, positioning and strategy.

Bosses must not simply have enormous health bars.

They must have distinct attack patterns, phases, weaknesses and mechanics.

==================================================
6. MONSTERS AND CREATURES

Create a large ecosystem of fantasy creatures.

Creature categories:

- Common monsters.
- Uncommon monsters.
- Rare monsters.
- Elite monsters.
- Named monsters.
- Legendary monsters.
- Unique world bosses.

Monsters should have:

- Individual behaviors.
- Territories.
- Different levels of aggression.
- Hunting patterns.
- Environmental preferences.
- Distinct combat abilities.

Some creatures should be extremely difficult to discover.

Rare monsters must not simply be stronger versions of ordinary enemies.

==================================================
7. BOSSES AND SECRET CONTENT

Create a deep hidden-content system.

Include:

- Secret bosses.
- Hidden dungeons.
- Legendary weapons.
- Forgotten civilizations.
- Secret quests.
- Unique achievements.
- Hidden class evolutions.
- Rare titles.

Some discoveries should require:

- Solving environmental puzzles.
- Exploring specific locations.
- Finding hidden objects.
- Completing unusual sequences of actions.
- Meeting particular NPCs.
- Defeating certain enemies.
- Discovering pieces of ancient lore.

Do not reveal every secret through map markers.

The community should be able to discover things together.

==================================================
8. LEVELING AND PROGRESSION

Implement a complete progression system.

Include:

- Character levels.
- Experience points.
- Attributes.
- Strength.
- Agility.
- Intelligence.
- Vitality.
- Dexterity.
- Wisdom.
- Luck.

Players must gain meaningful progression through different activities.

Combat, crafting, exploration and professions must all contribute to character development.

Avoid making leveling excessively repetitive.

==================================================
9. EQUIPMENT AND LOOT

Create an equipment system with different rarity levels:

- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.
- Mythical.
- Unique.

Equipment must have individual statistics and characteristics.

Include:

- Weapons.
- Armor.
- Helmets.
- Gloves.
- Boots.
- Accessories.
- Rings.
- Necklaces.
- Shields.

Some unique objects should have special abilities and individual lore.

Legendary equipment must feel genuinely special.

==================================================
10. CRAFTING AND PROFESSIONS

Implement meaningful professions:

- Blacksmithing.
- Alchemy.
- Cooking.
- Fishing.
- Mining.
- Herbalism.
- Enchanting.
- Tailoring.
- Woodworking.
- Beast taming.

Players should be able to specialize in professions.

High-level artisans should be capable of producing equipment that becomes famous across the world.

Crafting must have quality levels, materials, recipes and progression.

==================================================
11. ECONOMY AND PLAYER COMMERCE

Create a player-driven economy.

Include:

- Player marketplaces.
- Trading.
- Auctions.
- Merchant NPCs.
- Resource gathering.
- Equipment sales.
- Rare item exchanges.

Allow players to specialize as merchants.

Economic activity should have meaningful consequences.

If multiplayer trading is not supported, implement a functional local economy prototype without pretending it is online.

==================================================
12. NPC INTELLIGENCE

NPCs must have believable behaviors.

Implement:

- Daily routines.
- Individual personalities.
- Dialogue.
- Relationships.
- Memory of player interactions where supported.
- Reputations.
- Faction affiliations.
- Reactions to world events.

NPCs should not all behave like identical quest dispensers.

Some should be merchants, guards, adventurers, rulers, artisans and ordinary inhabitants.

==================================================
13. GUILDS AND POLITICAL SYSTEM

Create a guild system.

Players should be able to:

- Create guilds.
- Invite members.
- Establish alliances.
- Compete with rival guilds.
- Participate in guild missions.
- Fight in organized battles.
- Control territories if supported.

Create different kingdoms and political factions.

World events should be able to change political relationships.

==================================================
14. WORLD EVENTS

The world must feel alive.

Examples:

- Dragon invasions.
- Monster migrations.
- Kingdom wars.
- Ancient dungeon discoveries.
- Merchant caravans.
- Rare creature appearances.
- Natural disasters.
- Seasonal festivals.
- World boss encounters.

Events should offer meaningful rewards and create memorable experiences.

==================================================
15. MULTIPLAYER ARCHITECTURE

The long-term target is a real online MMORPG.

Plan for:

- Player accounts.
- Persistent characters.
- Online multiplayer.
- Shared world instances.
- Multiplayer combat.
- Parties.
- Guilds.
- Player trading.
- Server-authoritative progression.
- Persistent inventories.
- Shared world events.

IMPORTANT TECHNICAL RULE:

Do not simulate multiplayer with fake NPC players.

If real online networking, persistent servers or account systems are not supported by the current development environment, clearly identify the limitation.

Build a modular single-player prototype that can later be connected to real multiplayer infrastructure.

==================================================
16. USER INTERFACE

Create a professional MMORPG interface.

Include:

- Character health bar.
- Mana bar.
- Experience bar.
- Level display.
- Skill hotbar.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Character attributes.
- Quest tracker.
- Mini-map.
- World map.
- Settings.
- NPC interaction interface.

The interface must support Android touchscreen controls and adapt to different screen sizes.

Also support keyboard and mouse when available.

==================================================
17. VISUAL QUALITY AND PERFORMANCE

Use immersive 3D fantasy graphics.

Prioritize:

- Detailed environments.
- Distinctive character designs.
- Good lighting.
- Atmospheric effects.
- Smooth animations.
- Readable combat effects.
- Consistent artistic direction.

Optimize for Android devices.

Use level-of-detail systems and efficient asset management where supported.

Maintain a stable frame rate.

==================================================
18. SAVE SYSTEM

Implement persistent progression.

Save:

- Character information.
- Level.
- Experience.
- Skills.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Quest progress.
- Discovered locations.
- Achievements.

Use reliable storage supported by the platform.

Do not claim that cloud synchronization exists unless it is actually implemented.

==================================================
19. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Build the game in functional stages.

FIRST:
Create a playable 3D environment with a controllable character, third-person camera and working movement.

SECOND:
Implement combat, enemies, health, damage and experience.

THIRD:
Implement inventory, equipment, leveling and quests.

FOURTH:
Create NPCs, merchants, dungeons and bosses.

FIFTH:
Add professions, crafting, hidden classes and world events.

SIXTH:
Implement and test real multiplayer infrastructure if technically supported.

Do not create non-functional menus or placeholder buttons.

If a feature cannot be implemented, explain why and identify what is needed.

==================================================
20. FINAL VISION

ETERIA must become a living fantasy universe.

A player should be able to spend hundreds of hours exploring, fighting, crafting, trading, discovering secrets and building relationships.

Two players should be able to experience completely different adventures.

There should always be something new to discover.

The ultimate objective is to create a technically functional, visually immersive, expandable fantasy MMORPG with its own identity, world, lore and community.

Prioritize actual playable systems, technical stability and meaningful player freedom above empty promises and decorative features.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
